steps.say: This lesson shows how the system is built: the main Makefile targets, the base system, and where the output goes. It only shows where things are and runs nothing. Builds run inside WSL or Linux.
Everything is built into build/. That gives the kernel, build/kernel.elf; the OS's own files, build/initrd.cpio; the base system, build/base.cpio; and the bootable image, build/os.iso.
`make kernel` builds only the kernel, using kernel/Makefile. It is the quickest check that kernel code compiles.

steps.through: cd $(BUILD)/initrd && find . | LC_ALL=C sort | cpio -o -H newc --quiet > ../initrd.cpio
steps.say: `initrd` builds user space (init, os-shell and the tools) and packs it, with userland/rootfs, into one cpio archive. A cpio archive is a plain bundle of files that the kernel unpacks at boot.

steps.anchor: SHELL_OBJS := $(patsubst %.c,$(OUT)/obj/%.o,$(wildcard shell/*.c shell/fm/*.c shell/wl/*.c shell/fx/*.c shell/m3d/*.c))
steps.say: Every .c file in these folders becomes part of os-shell automatically. A new file there needs no Makefile change.
`make` (the same as `make iso`) makes the release image: kernel, initrd, base system, the built-in model if there is one, and the Limine bootloader. It boots with UEFI and with BIOS.

steps.anchor: # For development: the system in two discs. dev.iso (tens of MB, rebuilt in seconds) holds the kernel, the OS
steps.through: # exactly as from the one release image (make iso). BIOS only, as the VMs boot.
steps.say: For everyday work there is `make dev-iso`. The small disc is rebuilt in seconds, and the big files sit on a second disc, big.iso, which is rebuilt only when they change.
The base system is the Freedesktop Platform that Flatpak apps run on, plus what it lacks. It is built separately, rarely, and installed into ~/osbuild/base.

steps.anchor: # The OS's base system: the Freedesktop Platform runtime (the same
steps.through: # org.freedesktop.Sdk//26.08 runtime installed for this user.
steps.say: scripts/build-base.sh builds each part from source: bubblewrap, D-Bus, OSTree, Flatpak, llama.cpp, whisper.cpp and more. You can build one part at a time by giving its name.

`make run` boots the image in QEMU in WSL with a 1 GB disk of its own. On Windows, Operating System.cmd starts it in Windows QEMU instead. First scripts/launcher.ps1 shows a small window of choices, then scripts/os-win.ps1 starts the VM.
build/ is never committed. Logs, test output and screenshots all land there, and build/tmp is free for scratch files.
